text:
Dear Professor Linden,

On behalf of the programme committee, I am delighted to invite you to give a plenary lecture at the International Symposium on Sustainable Materials, to be held in Lisbon from 8 to 10 September. [1] Your recent paper on biodegradable composites generated considerable discussion among committee members, and we believe that it would be of great interest to delegates.

The symposium will cover the cost of your accommodation for three nights and will [2] your airfare up to a maximum of €800. We should be grateful if you could let us know by 15 April [3] you are able to accept, so that your name can be included in the preliminary program. If you wish to [4] a coauthor or a student to the symposium, please inform us, and we shall endeavor to arrange a reduced registration fee.

Yours sincerely,
Beatriz Calado

choices: Your reputation in the field is such that we regard your participation as essential to the success of the event.
Your reputation in the field is such that we regard your participation as unnecessary to the success of the event.
Our reputation in the field is such that we regard the event as essential to the success of your participation.
Your reputation in the field was such that we regarded your participation as essential to the success of the event.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says that the paper generated discussion and would interest delegates, supporting a sentence about the speaker's standing; only the first is coherent.
The symposium will 'reimburse' airfare, meaning repay it; the other verbs do not fit.
'Let us know whether you are able to accept' introduces an indirect yes/no question; 'that' would not.
One may 'accompany' a coauthor, meaning bring along; the others do not fit.

text:
Smaller Firms Embrace Four-Day Trials

A growing number of small businesses are experimenting with a four-day working week, [1] fears that productivity will suffer. Among them is Calderwood Print, a firm of thirty employees, which reduced its week to thirty-two hours last spring without a cut in pay. [2] Its managing director, Laura Voss, reports that output has held steady, while absenteeism has fallen by a quarter.

Critics, [3], doubt that the model can be applied across the economy. Roles that require constant availability, such as those in customer support, are difficult to [4] without additional staff. Ms. Voss concedes the point, but says that the experiment has been worthwhile for her own company.

questions.explanation: 'Despite fears that productivity will suffer' expresses concession; the others express cause.

choices: The results of the trial, which ended in September, have so far fallen short of the expectations of management.
The results of the trial, which ends in September, have so far greatly exceeded the expectations of management.
The results of the staff, which ends in September, have so far exceeded the expectations of the trial.
The cost of the trial, which ends in September, has so far exceeded the expectations of the staff.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reports positive results from the managing director, so the previous one must introduce favorable results; only the first does.
The critics' doubt contrasts with the positive results; 'however' marks the contrast.
Roles of constant availability are difficult to 'cover' with fewer staff, meaning staff adequately; the others do not fit.
